purpose: Use contrasting occupational requirements to discover shared foundations and recursively ask how those foundations can be learned from earlier starting points. Routes are test cases for the learning structure.

routes.label: domestic cleaner — foundation exploration

stages.label: 1. Supported early foundations
stages.description: No prior learning records required. A familiar supporter offers play, communication access, choices and co-regulation. These are possible entry points, not an age test.

stages.label: 2. Shared practical foundations
stages.description: Develop communication, reading, quantities, safe action and planning through repeated supported practice. Different access methods and help remain valid.

stages.label: 3. domestic cleaner: contextual practice
stages.description: All essential ESCO requirements are accounted for. Existing draft leaves are retained; contextual exercises keep occupational assessment expectations distinct. Missing canonical breakdowns remain blocking gaps.

routes.scope: Explore the foundations behind every essential ESCO 1.2.1 requirement for domestic cleaner. A contextual exercise does not fill a missing canonical breakdown or establish job readiness.
routes.semantics: Every listed input is required (AND). Gates aggregate evidence and cannot be ticked complete. Missing canonical activity breakdowns block the affected branch even after its contextual exercise. Adult life is a separate pathway, not an occupational prerequisite.
routes.access: Use speech, sign, AAC, accessible text, assistive tools and agreed human support. Adapt the activity and record the assistance used. There is no fixed age or duration; early tasks are supporter-mediated, and adult/work scenarios are for an appropriate later context.
review_needed: Review shared-foundation and intermediate prerequisite hypotheses with learning and accessibility specialists
Review domestic cleaner tasks, source-skill breadth and supplied procedures with a practitioner
Add missing intermediate practice and record limits of transfer between contexts

breakdowns.source_definition: Notify customers on new promotional actions and special offers.
breakdowns.boundary: Use supplied fictional campaign records, prices, validity periods and communication permissions. No marketing-law interpretation or real customer contact.
breakdowns.remaining: Review campaign/channel variation, communication access and local authorisation rules with a retail practitioner; the examples do not establish independent sales competence.

facets.label: New promotional actions and special offers
Notify customers using an appropriate accessible message

breakdowns.source_definition: Maintain updated the statutory books of the company with the relevant information of the directors and secretaries, the directors interests, and the register of shareholders.
breakdowns.boundary: All people, companies, registers and authorities in the exercise are fictional. Apply only the supplied procedure; no real filing, deadlines, legal interpretation or claim of compliance.
breakdowns.remaining: An authorised company-records practitioner must review jurisdiction, company type, required fields, evidence, retention/access and real-world responsibilities. The draft covers the categories named in ESCO, not every statutory obligation.

breakdowns.source_definition: Answer questions, resolve doubts, and solve inquiries in regard to general institutional and corporate information such as program rules, regulations and procedures. Assist with information to both, employees and public at large.
breakdowns.boundary: Use a fictional institution/company, approved information pack and supplied authority/access rules. No real disclosure or interpretation of actual regulations.
breakdowns.remaining: Review information ownership, accessibility, difficult enquiries and organisation-specific boundaries. A correct supplied-case response does not demonstrate every type of enquiry can be resolved.

facets.label: Answer general institutional and corporate questions

breakdowns.source_definition: XML-based information systems that allows for direct interactions between applications through Internet. It is a set of protocols for transferring data between applications and systems.
breakdowns.boundary: ESCO 1.2.1 defines this knowledge concept as XML-based inter-application exchange. Use inert XML/WSDL/SOAP examples and local mocks; no external service, credentials or untrusted XML execution.
breakdowns.remaining: Review XML/schema breadth, other service versions/bindings, interoperability and security in real systems. Recognising these supplied examples does not establish production integration or secure deployment competence.

facets.label: Compatibility and limits of the supplied exchange

groups.label: Reading and practical messages
groups.aim: Connect written forms with meaning, interpret a short instruction, locate document fields and produce a checked record. A taught decoding method or accessible reader is recorded explicitly.
groups.remaining: Language-specific decoding progressions, vocabulary breadth, longer-text comprehension and the support needed still need specialist review.

groups.label: Quantities, measurement and scaling
groups.aim: Separate grouping/counting, repeated units, scale readings, estimates, equal parts, simple fractions, decimals, scale factors and time. Use each branch where the context needs it.
groups.remaining: Unit conversion, diverse fractions, numerical fluency and occupational precision beyond the supplied models remain undeveloped.

groups.label: Sequences, state and testing
groups.aim: Build a sequence from action inputs, check conditions, track repetitions, update named values, predict results and replay failures before connecting card rules to code.
groups.remaining: Generalisation to larger programs, nested rules and independent problem-solving requires more practice and review.

refinement.learning_records: Earlier completion records are retained. A revised activity counts as complete in a route only after every newly specified input is complete; earlier completion alone is not evidence for the added practice.

findings.title: Checking is shared; acceptance criteria remain contextual
findings.detail: Cleaning a surface, receiving ingredients and debugging a program all compare observations with expected results. The proposed observation and evidence activities are reused, while the supplied criteria and occupational demonstrations stay separate.

findings.title: Quantity branches need more than counting
findings.detail: Stock counting, cooking portions and expense tables reveal different next steps: units and measurement, scaling relationships, and structured records. Added measure, proportion and table activities make those distinctions inspectable.

findings.title: A short routine is not yet a development process
findings.detail: Software requirements expose missing reasoning layers: conditional rules, repetition, state, problem decomposition, interfaces and tests. Each now has an observable draft activity with explicit earlier inputs.

findings.title: Documents and handovers reveal shared information structure
findings.detail: Retail orders, office case files and kitchen handovers reuse recording identifiers, status, ownership and next action. Audience and access boundaries remain explicit rather than assuming all information can be shared.

findings.title: Same ESCO skill does not imply identical occupational assessment
findings.detail: The comparison lists exact shared source-skill IDs separately from proposed foundations. Each occupation retains its own contextual demonstration, so completing a retail example does not automatically satisfy the shelf-filling or administration example.

questions.title: How much numerical breadth and precision do the contexts need?
questions.detail: Repeated units, scale readings, estimates, equal parts, simple fractions, decimals and scale factors now have smaller draft activities. Unit conversion, numerical fluency, varied fractions and tool-specific precision still need decomposition and practitioner review.

questions.title: Which reading strategies and support are needed beyond these examples?
questions.detail: Written-form matching, meaning checks, supported word reading, sentence meaning, instructions, document fields and short records now have separate practice. Language-specific decoding sequences, vocabulary breadth and longer texts remain open; accessible reading is distinguished from unaided decoding.

questions.title: What transfers from small explicit rules to larger programs?
questions.detail: Condition checks, branch outcomes, counted repetition, stop conditions, single updates, traces, expected results and failure replay are now separate. The code bridge compares physical rules with supplied constructs; nested rules and independent generalisation still need investigation.

questions.title: What is missing between safe mock practice and real tools?
questions.detail: Reach, grip, sensory feedback, fatigue and environmental variation need individual exploration. Mock exercises intentionally leave sharp, hot, powered and chemical practice for appropriate instruction and supervision.

questions.title: Which proposed inputs are prerequisites, practice aids or alternatives?
questions.detail: The current route engine treats listed inputs as AND. Review whether each is necessary, whether order can change, and which accessible alternatives should replace a requirement. Usage counts measure this authored model, not causal evidence.
